labels.label: bbsdef:singular_hs_surface_oriented_surface
labels.notes: I read GX.IsSingularHSSurface (HSSuspension.lean:1459) against colI_v1.tex:948-953 one clause at a time. (1) « surface »: IsTopologicalSurface M, which is OQ-104's reading (OQ-104 is OPEN in registers/DECISIONS.md:327), named. (2) « oriented »: not a field, a named reading. This is sound: the HS-structure orients Σ∖𝒮 (l.621-623), that orientation extends over a closed discrete 𝒮, and mathlib at the pin has no orientations of topological manifolds. (3) « discrete subset 𝒮 »: DiscreteTopology A.sing, carried. That 𝒮 is closed is derived from support_eq (isClosed_sing). (4) « Σ∖𝒮 is a regular HS-surface »: SingularHSStructure gives a gxGroupoid-compatible atlas of partial charts of Σ whose support is exactly 𝒮ᶜ. With T2 from (1), isHSSurface_reg yields the strict GX.IsHSSurface on regOpens. Carried. (5) « every p ∈ 𝒮 admits a neighborhood HS-isomorphic to an open subset of 𝔢(L) of a (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle L »: there exist L : Type, C : GammaLinkCircle L, Δ : C.DevData, and an OpenPartialHomeomorph φ : M → BiSusp L with x ∈ φ.source and IsIso A Δ.suspStructure φ. IsIso (l.923-927) is not degenerate. φ.source is an open neighbourhood of x and φ.target is open. Clause 1 matches the singular sets, so x goes to an apex and regular points go to regular points. Clause 2 asks for an element of SO₀(1,2) (Causal.Flat.lorentz 2 is SO₀(1,2): det 1, preserves the future cone) in any pair of charts near every regular point of the source. This is the strict gx morphism condition (it is literally GX.IsRegularOn.exists_smul_eq), not a vacuous one. The readings are named in the REPORT questions: the matching reading of « HS-isomorphic », p overloaded (finding 1), and Δ existential. I checked the closer's argument that the matching reading equals the no-matching reading, via regular_susp: it holds. I also checked the Δ-independence argument: two equivariant lifts differ by κ w + μ p with κ > 0 and κ, μ 1-periodic, and the segment reparametrisation is a homeomorphism fixing the ends. It holds as well. 𝔢(L) itself is faithful to l.775-781. suspAtlas consists of cone charts over charts of L's maximal (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-atlas (mem_maximalAtlas_of_mem_suspAtlas). Each segment {σ}×[0,π] goes onto 𝔢(c σ) (range_suspMap_mk). The chart changes are the same elements g_ij ∈ Γ_p as L's (suspAtlas_eventually_eq_smul), so the regular part is ⊔𝔢(U_i)∖{±p}/g_ij, as SCOPE (a) argues. Witnesses: every HS-surface (𝒮 = ∅), and every 𝔢(L) with 𝒮 = poles = {north, south}, two distinct points (north_ne_south), so the singular clause is exercised with 𝒮 ≠ ∅. The 𝔢(L) witness is the refl map with isIso_refl, which is legitimate. Neither witness exhibits a non-removable singular point, and for L = ℓ(p) the apices are removable (regular_susp). The paper's definition does not require 𝒮 to be minimal, and SCOPE (h) discloses that singularity of the apices for L ≇ ℓ(p) is not formalized. Status partial and unmarked: correct, since the mark waits on OQ-104 and three further readings. The module docstring (first 4000 characters) has no **`label`** mark; see the minor finding on the declaration docstring at l.1455. The other theorems are universal over Δ (isHSSurface_reg, regular_susp, isSingularHSSurface), so nothing in them is narrower than the paper.

findings.what: Finding 2 says the paper's « topologically a sphere » is « now proved » (« The statement is true: GX.GammaLinkCircle.suspHomeomorph »), and the notes say « every assertion of the 𝔢(L) prose is proved ». What is formal is that the coordinate model BiSusp L, with suspStructure Δ, is a sphere. That this model is the paper's quotient ⊔𝔢(U_i)/∼ is argued, not formalized (SCOPE (a), (g)). The apices are not shown singular when L ≇ ℓ(p) (SCOPE (h)). Finding 2 also calls the proof « not routine ». That is a judgement: the regular part is an interval bundle over the circle whose structure group preserves the orientation of the segments, so it is trivial. The mathematical content of the finding is true: the paper gives no proof, and no Γ_p-equivariant trivialisation exists at a non-time-like p, which I checked for the boost, and for the parabolic at a light-like p, [ap + be] ↦ [(a + sb)p + be].
findings.fix: Reword finding 2: « stated without proof; proved for the coordinate model, whose identity with the paper's quotient is argued (SCOPE (a)) ». Drop « not routine », or replace it with the specific obstruction (no Γ_p-equivariant product chart). Qualify « every assertion proved » in the notes the same way.

findings.where: REPORT.json findings[4] (l.641-644, one g_ij per overlap)
findings.what: The finding is overstated. It is true only for atlases with disconnected overlaps, such as two arcs covering a circle. An atlas whose pairwise overlaps are connected always exists: three arcs for a circle, a good cover for a surface. With such an atlas there is one g_ij per overlap, and with no triple overlaps on the circle no cocycle is needed. So the paper's « can be understood as » is correct for a suitable atlas. Sent as stated, the finding would tell the author his construction is defective when it is at most imprecise.
findings.fix: Rephrase it as a precision remark: the description needs an atlas with connected overlaps, which always exists, or chart changes local to each component (gx's convention). Alternatively, drop it.

findings.what: Reuse is not addressed for two strict notions, both already in scope through GX.BBS.IPm. (a) IsIso's chart clause is verbatim the field exists_smul_eq of GX.IsRegularOn (GX/Singular/Atlas.lean:568). SingularHSStructure parallels gx's a.e. atlases (GX.IsAEAtlas, GX.SingularGXStructure), with no bridge lemma and no SCOPE line saying why it differs: BBS's 𝒮 is a datum that may contain removable points, while gx's Sing is intrinsic; and gx's IsGXAtlas works on connected components while gxGroupoid is local. (b) The BBS L0 suspension céleste (GX.ConicStructure, GX.ConicChart.celestialAtlas; GX/Suspension/Conic.lean:359, Celestial.lean) is not mentioned. It cannot serve here: its map_smul is a Γ_p-equivariant radial trivialisation, which SCOPE (a) itself shows does not exist at a non-time-like p. That is worth stating, and worth reporting to the author as a limit of L0's ConicStructure for (SO₀(1,2), HS²). The CAMPAIGN « Reuse » rule and the dispatch both ask for this.
findings.fix: Restate IsIso's second clause as GX.IsRegularOn (Causal.Flat.lorentz 2) A.atlas B.atlas φ (φ.source ∩ A.singᶜ), or prove the two equivalent.
